title: Dashcam Shows Car Chase & Gunfight Following Attack of Greenville Police Officer
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Greenville, South Carolina — On January 11th, 2026, around 1:50 a.m., a Greenville Police officer parked in the front parking lot of the Greenville County Law Enforcement Center located at 4 McGee St. was ambushed in a targeted attack by a suspect with a shotgun. That suspect has since been identified as 42-year-old David William Lane. Following the attack, deputies at the law enforcement center rendered aid to the injured police officer and worked to identify and locate the suspect who was seen driving away in a 2019 silver Honda Civic. At approximately 3:15 a.m., a Greenville County deputy located the suspect's vehicle on Roper Mountain Road and followed the vehicle until it turned on Huntington Road and stopped. 

As the deputy observed the suspect's actions, the suspect fired multiple rounds at the deputy from two different locations. The deputy did not return fire. Following the series of gunfire from the suspect, deputies saturated the area and ultimately pursued the suspect to a parking lot near the intersection of Independence Boulevard and Ponders Road. The suspect stopped his vehicle and opened fire again on deputies. One deputy returned fire before the suspect drove away and quickly turned into a nearby parking lot. Once in the parking lot, the suspect was forcibly stopped and an officer involved shooting occurred. Following the shooting, the suspect was pronounced deceased by what the Greenville County Coroner's Office revealed was a self-inflicted gunshot that occurred around the time of the forcible stop. The suspect's 12- gauge shotgun and 9mm handgun were collected from the scene and seized as evidence.
